text:
jia: Quick sync — want to lock the Embeddings MVP contract so eng can start implementation. Main asks: batching limits, per-item metadata, partial-failure semantics, model selection heuristic, and launch gates.

mike: +1. Can we keep this tight? customers expect both single-shot and bulk upload.

sara: Proposal: MVP supports input arrays up to 5k items per request, but enforce 10MB payload cap and 30s processing timeout. Single-item case should be cheap and low-latency.

ianil: 5k seems high for first rollout. Service cost + memory spikes. Can we do staged caps: 500 for GA, 5k behind Dedicated/reserved?

jia: I like staged. GA = 500 items, burst-mode flag for 5k on Dedicated. Documented quotas and rate limits.

emily: Response format: each input must accept an optional client_id, and we return per-item status + either embedding or error string. Example snippet:```json
{
  "data": [
    {"client_id":"row-1","embedding":[0.1, -0.02, ...],"status":"ok","model":"redwood-emb-small"},
    {"client_id":"row-2","error":"text too long","status":"error"}
  ],
  "model":"redwood-emb-small-v1",
  "request_id":"abc123"
}
```

mike: Important: include model in each item? maybe top-level model is enough. But per-item model field helps when we fall back to a different model for some inputs.

sara: We plan auto-routing: short docs -> small model, long docs -> large model. If fallback happens mid-batch, we must surface which rows used fallback. So per-item model recommended.

ianil: Also need deterministic ids to make retries idempotent. Recommend clients pass client_ids; if missing, server generates but warns.

emily: Metadata fields to return: tokens_processed, cost_estimate (optional), and quantization_info (if applicable). Those help billing + debugging.

jia: Launch gates (MVP): 1) API contract + doc pages complete, 2) E2E perf for single-item median latency < 120ms on hosted small model, bulk 500-item p95 < 5s under typical load, 3) graceful partial failures with clear error codes, 4) telemetry: per-request token counts and model-routing logs, 5) at least two pilot customers signed for GA.

mike: Can ops guarantee autoscale for 500-item bursts? If not, reduce GA cap.

ianil: Ops: we'll support autoscale but warm pools required. Recommend burst window and queueing. We'll provide a queue-length header so clients can back off.

sara: API surface: POST /v1/embeddings accepts {model?, inputs: [{text:, client_id?:, metadata?:{}}], batch_options?:{priority:, allow_fallback:bool, prefer_small:bool}}. Returning per-item entries as above.

emily: Edge cases: 1) mixed-length batch where some items exceed per-item token limit -> those should return error per-item, not fail whole request. 2) partial success must have 207-like behavior. We should adopt HTTP 207 Multi-Status semantics but keep JSON shape above.

mike: minor nit: 207 is fine but many SDKs don't expect it. Maybe always 200 with top-level summary status and per-item statuses?

sara: Agreed — always 200 for API simplicity, include top-level "overall_status": "partial"|"ok"|"failed" and per-item statuses.

emily: Model selection heuristic doc (draft): if avg tokens < 256 -> redwood-emb-small (dim 768), else -> redwood-emb-large (dim 1536). Allow a query param "force_model" to override.

ianil: Customers asked for consistent embedding dims per endpoint. Can we offer endpoint-level pinning (endpoint returns embeddings of a fixed dimension)?

sara: Yes — we should support endpoint-level model pin (e.g., /v1/endpoints/emb-prod -> always 1536). For the multi-model auto route we return per-item model and normalize dims into distinct fields (embedding_768 or embedding_1536) or better: return embedding + dimension field.

emily: Return shape example: {"embedding": [...], "dim": "1536"}. SDKs will need to validate length.

mike: Backwards compatibility: defaulting to 1536 might break some customers. Default keep small (768) for cheaper ops, but make migration docs clear.

ianil: Monitoring/alerts: surface sudden shifts in average embedding dimension per-customer (could indicate misuse) and high error rates per-item.

emily: On rollout: plan canary to 2 internal teams, then 3 pilot customers, then GA with staged quota increases. Rollback flags: model-pin revert and batch-cap reduction.

jia: Action items: - @sara write API contract draft PR (due EOD Thu) - @anil ops run memory/cost sim for 500 vs 5k bursts (due Mon) - @mike SDK owners draft client retry/idempotency patterns (due Fri) - @emily add example responses + partial-failure RFC in docs site (due Thu)

deploy-bot: Created PR #482: "embeddings: MVP API contract + response examples" by sara.

mike: Thanks everyone — want a follow-up after PR so we can sign off on GA criteria. :thumbsup:
